content.title: About
content.content: Quesadilla with egg and meat is a Mexican dish consisting of a thin corn or wheat tortilla filled with scrambled egg and sautéed meat (usually beef or chicken). It is quick to prepare, filling, and rich in protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The quesadilla originated in central Mexico as a convenient way to use leftover meat and eggs.
Traditionally cheese is added, but in the egg‑and‑meat version cheese is often omitted or used sparingly.
The dish is popular at street stalls and fast‑food outlets because it can be assembled and cooked in minutes.
In the United States quesadillas are commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs and meat provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and meat are abundant in B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: When made with corn tortillas the carbohydrate load remains moderate, fitting low‑carb diets.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Meat provides zinc, important for immune function and wound healing.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Fatty cuts of meat can raise cholesterol levels, so lean options are recommended.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to egg whites and should avoid the dish.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If sauces or pre‑made seasonings are added, the sodium level may become high.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Meat must be fully cooked and eggs cooked until firm to prevent salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Quesadilla is conveniently eaten by hand, cut into wedges. Serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or a squeeze of fresh lime. Add fresh veggies such as tomatoes, avocado, or lettuce for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared quesadilla in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave to restore a crisp crust.
